data.narrative: Led the performance investigation with profilers and runtime probes before reading code. The fork already hardens the canonical leaks (sessions close in finally, /links fires 3 statements), so the tool data redirected attention to the genuinely present issues: cache clients acquired without guaranteed release, and unbounded long_url input that scales CPU linearly with attacker-controlled size.

dimension_scores.observation: Formed hypotheses tied to specific probes before touching code, and each probe produced a falsifiable result.
dimension_scores.evidence: Latency-scaling probe showed linear growth across URL lengths, falsifying the catastrophic-backtracking hypothesis for this fork.

dimension_scores.observation: Used runtime output (tracemalloc allocations, SQL statement counts, CLIENT LIST) as the primary narrative source rather than relying on error logs.
dimension_scores.evidence: SQL listener showed exactly 3 statements on /links; tracemalloc showed no growing DB connection objects.

dimension_scores.observation: Built four reproducible probes that anyone can rerun and see the same numbers.
dimension_scores.evidence: probe_memory.py, probe_conn_leak.py, probe_n1.py, probe_cpu_scale.py each isolate one variable and print deterministic output.

dimension_scores.observation: Documented each finding with evidence files and tool output at every step.
dimension_scores.evidence: evidence/module-04/evidence.txt and break_evidence.txt capture probe output verbatim.

dimension_scores.observation: Did not stop at 'no leak detected'; traced the residual acquire-without-guaranteed-release pattern and the unbounded-input resource-exhaustion vector.
dimension_scores.evidence: Fixed cache.py client lifecycle with finally blocks and capped long_url at 2048 chars.

dimension_scores.observation: Clear findings and fixes, but no formal blameless writeup with owner-backed remediations.
dimension_scores.evidence: Evidence files document impact and root cause; remediation owner/checklist absent.

strengths: Used runtime tooling (tracemalloc, SQL event listener, live latency scaling) before reading source, per the module's rule.
Interpreted profiler output honestly: when the fork was already hardened, the data redirected to real remaining issues instead of forcing a false positive.
Applied the module's preferred fix combination (URL parser + input length cap) and verified rejection in milliseconds.
growth_areas: A formal blameless postmortem with remediation owners would complete the picture.
The cache client lifecycle was identified by code-reading after the probes showed no leak; an instrumented CLIENT LIST under induced Redis failure earlier would have isolated it sooner.
data.recommendation: Write a one-paragraph postmortem for the resource-exhaustion vector (impact, root cause, remediation, owner) and add a load test that sends oversized URLs to CI.

public_evidence.student_action: Moved aioredis client close into finally blocks in all three cache functions so connections release on every exit path.
public_evidence.technical_detail: get_redirect_target/set_redirect_target/invalidate_redirect_target now use a single client + finally aclose() instead of close-only-on-success.
public_evidence.proof: probe_conn_leak.py: Redis CLIENT LIST stayed at baseline (1) across 5 forced error-path rounds.
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Proves the candidate can spot acquire-without-guaranteed-release patterns and fix them with finally semantics.

public_evidence.student_action: Added a 2048-char max_length cap after the latency-scaling probe showed CPU/memory grow linearly with unbounded input.
public_evidence.technical_detail: schemas/link.py: long_url str = Field(max_length=2048); validation uses urllib.parse.urlparse (no regex).
public_evidence.proof: probe_cpu_scale.py: 25..100,019-char URLs returned in 7-16ms (linear); 2049-char rejected with string_too_long, full suite 74 tests exit 0.
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Demonstrates understanding that unbounded input is a resource-exhaustion vector even without regex backtracking, and applies defense-in-depth.
